items.title: The most iconic seafood shack in every state
items.summary: From roadside lobster rolls to clam shacks, here's the most iconic seafood shack in every state to try this summer. Jen Lobo/Getty Images Some of these iconic seafood spots have been family-run for generations. Others have become famous for their fresh catches or waterfront locations. These legendary seafood shacks are among the best in the country. Seafood shacks have long been a staple of American dining, from the rocky shores of Maine to coastal California locales. While there's bound to be some debate about which seafood shack is the most iconic in every state, we devised this list based on customer reviews, local history , cultural significance, and lasting reputation. And while the most celebrated seafood shacks are often located near waterfronts, in landlocked states we identified locally beloved seafood eateries that serve up a similar laid-back spirit. From legendary institutions like Woodman's of Essex in Massachusetts, credited with popularizing the fried clam, to classic crab boil establishments that have welcomed diners for decades, these are the most iconic seafood shacks in every state. ALABAMA: Doc's Seafood Shack & Oyster Bar in Orange Beach Doc's Seafood Shack & Oyster Bar. PizzaTheHut X./Yelp Since opening in 1984, Doc's Seafood Shack & Oyster Bar has proven that great seafood doesn't need a fancy setting. The laid-back spot is best known for its crispy fried shrimp — which the restaurant boldly bills as the best in the world — along with seafood gumbo, raw oysters, and build-your-own seafood platters piled high with Gulf Coast favorites. Voted by Fox News as one of the top 10 seafood shacks in America, it's been a longtime favorite for Alabama locals and tourists. ALASKA: Tracy's King Crab Shack in Juneau Tracy's King Crab Shack. Diana J./Yelp Few restaurants are as synonymous with Alaska seafood as Tracy's King Crab Shack. What started as a tiny dockside stand in 2006 has grown into one of Juneau's best-known seafood stops, beloved by the cruise crowd that rolls through the city in search of authentic Alaskan seafood. The menu is intentionally simple, letting the sweet crab take center stage, though the rich crab bisque is nearly as famous. ARIZONA: Chula Seafood in Phoenix Chula Seafood Uptown. Jeremy F./Yelp A seafood shack may seem out of place in the desert, but Chula Seafood has built its reputation by bringing boat-to-table fresh seafood to the city of Phoenix. Operated by a family of commercial fishermen, the restaurant has its own San Diego-based fishing boat, giving the menu a level of freshness that is rare for a landlocked state. The eatery also sources seafood from other domestic and international fisheries. ARKANSAS: The Oyster Bar in Little Rock The Oyster Bar. Carmen S./Yelp The Oyster Bar has been serving Little Rock since 1975, making it one of Arkansas' longest-running seafood restaurants. While its atmosphere is a bit more elevated than a traditional seafood shack, its honest, simple cooking and decades-long run have cemented it as a Little Rock institution and earned it a spot on this list. CALIFORNIA: Neptune's Net in Malibu Neptune's Net. Sam M./Yelp Neptune's Net has been perched along the Pacific Coast Highway since the 1950s, and it has even appeared in major Hollywood films like "The Fast and the Furious." Diners come for fried seafood, clam chowder, fish and chips , sandwiches, and fish tacos while soaking up sweeping ocean views that have made Neptune's Net one of the state's most recognizable seafood stops. COLORADO: Big Mac and Little Lu's Seafood Restaurant in Westminster Big Mac & Little Lu's Seafood Restaurant. Bonni R./Yelp In a state better known for steaks than seafood, Big Mac & Little Lu's has become a Colorado favorite by flying in fresh seafood several times a week. Open since 2013, the restaurant has built a devoted following for its fresh New England-style lobster rolls, crispy crab cakes, clam chowder, and classic fish and chips. The restaurant's longevity and reputation for fresh seafood in landlocked Colorado have made it a standout seafood spot. CONNECTICUT: Abbott's Lobster in the Rough in Noank Abbott's Lobster In the Rough. Ian L./Yelp For generations, Abbott's Lobster in the Rough has defined the classic New England seafood shack experience. Operating seasonally on the Mystic River since 1947, it serves up an overflowing hot Connecticut lobster roll, packed with warm lobster meat and served with drawn butter, but it also offers Maine versions dressed with mayonnaise. Picnic tables overlooking the water, steamed clams, chowder, and a rich maritime history have made going to Abbott's one of Connecticut's most beloved summer traditions. DELAWARE: JR's Seafood Shack in Fenwick Island JR's Seafood Shack. Josh T./Yelp Just steps from the Delaware-Maryland line, JR's Seafood Shack has earned a loyal following by serving fresh local seafood without the fuss of a high-end restaurant, but a bit more elevated than the typical roadside seafood shack. The casual roadside stop is known for calamari, crab dip, steamed seafood, and low-country boils, making it a favorite stop for beachgoers headed to Fenwick Island. FLORIDA: Star Fish Company in Cortez Star Fish Co Seafood Market and Restaurant. Kaitlyn S./Yelp Star Fish Company feels like a glimpse into Old Florida. Operating as both a seafood market and a dockside restaurant in the historic fishing village of Cortez, the family-owned business serves whatever fresh catches local fishermen happen to bring in that day. Popular items include fresh grouper, fried fish, and Gulf shrimp, and its connection to the local fishing communities makes it one of the most authentic seafood shacks in the state. GEORGIA: The Crab Shack on Tybee Island The Crab Shack. Ray L./Yelp Billing itself as "where the elite eat in their bare feet," The Crab Shack has become one of Georgia's most iconic seafood destinations thanks to its sprawling waterfront setting and famously messy seafood boils. The quirky atmosphere — complete with wandering cats, alligators, and marsh views — has made it a must-visit for decades. HAWAII: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Oahu. Steven C./Yelp Few food trucks have achieved the legendary status of Giovanni's Shrimp Truck. What started as a humble roadside stand has since become a Hawaiian icon. Parked on O'ahu's North Shore since the early 1990s, the graffiti-covered truck helped popularize Hawaii's famous shrimp plate and now draws visitors from around the world for its buttery garlic shrimp over rice. It has two North Shore locations: the original location in Kahuku and a second, beloved spot in Hale'iwa. IDAHO: Fresh Off the Hook in Boise Fresh Off The Hook. Joe C./Yelp Fresh Off the Hook has spent decades proving Idaho can do excellent seafood despite being hundreds of miles from the coast. The family-owned restaurant flies in fresh seafood several times a week and serves everything from cedar plank salmon and ahi tuna to fish tacos and oysters. ILLINOIS: Calumet Fisheries in Chicago Calumet Fisheries. Izzy L./Yelp Few seafood shacks are as legendary as Calumet Fisheries, a James Beard award-winning restaurant that has been smoking fish over oak fires since 1948, though the original site and smokehouse date back 20 years earlier. Located beside the Calumet River on Chicago's Southeast Side, the no-frills smokehouse is famous for fried seafood as well as smoked shrimp, salmon, trout, and pepper-and-garlic smoked fish. INDIANA: Caplinger's Fresh Catch in Indianapolis Caplinger's Fresh Catch. Caplinger's Fresh Catch/Yelp Part seafood market, part casual restaurant, Caplinger's Fresh Catch has become Indiana's go-to destination for high-quality seafood. The family-owned business is known for lobster rolls, crab cakes, oysters, po'boys, and Seafood Philly, a mashup between a Philly cheesesteak and a lobster roll. IOWA: Waterfront Seafood Market in West Des Moines Waterfront Seafood Market. Todd B./Yelp Waterfront Seafood Market has served Iowans fresh seafood for more than 40 years, earning a reputation as the state's premier fish market and casual seafood restaurant. Diners come from far and wide to try the market's fresh sushi, peel-and-eat shrimp, fried seafood baskets, and crab cakes. KANSAS: Jarocho in Kansas City Jarocho. Chris L./Yelp Jarocho has earned national acclaim by bringing the flavors of Mexico's Veracruz coast to the Kansas City area. More polished than a traditional shack, its focus on high-quality seafood has made it a standout spot in the landlocked state. KENTUCKY: Mike Linnig's Famous Seafood Restaurant in Louisville Mike Linnig's Restaurant. Kelly J./Yelp Mike Linnig's has welcomed diners since the 1920s, making it one of Kentucky's oldest seafood restaurants. The sprawling outdoor beer garden and family-friendly atmosphere are as much a draw as the generous platters of classic Southern favorites like fried fish, frog legs, fried oysters, and peel-and-eat shrimp. LOUISIANA: Middendorf's in Manchac Middendorf's. Middendorf's/Yelp Open since 1934, Middendorf's has been one of Louisiana's oldest and most defining seafood restaurants, particularly famous for its thin-fried catfish. Though not a traditional shack, it serves up many of the classic items you'd expect to find in the bayou, from seafood gumbo to crawfish étouffée and fried shrimp. MAINE: The Clam Shack in Kennebunkport The Clam Shack. Rob M./Yelp The Clam Shack has been drawing summer crowds since 1968 with what many argue is one of the country's greatest lobster rolls , and a hallmark of Maine seafood. However, visitors might be surprised to learn that the Clam Shack doesn't specialize in Maine-style rolls. Unlike most versions, its roll features claw, knuckle, and tail meat lightly dressed with butter or mayonnaise and served on a round, locally baked bun. Along with whole-belly fried clams and waterfront views in Kennebunkport, it's become one of Maine's most celebrated seafood shacks. MARYLAND: The Crab Claw in St. Michaels The Crab Claw. Soojin J./Yelp The Crab Claw has overlooked St. Michaels Harbor since its opening in 1965, and is one of the Chesapeake Bay's most enduring crab houses. The restaurant has built its reputation on its famous steamed Maryland blue crabs coated in seasoning, along with classic crab cakes, oysters, soft-shell crabs, and cream of crab soup served in a casual atmosphere. MASSACHUSETTS: Woodman's of Essex in Essex Woodman's of Essex. Huy P./Yelp Few seafood shacks are as famous as Woodman's of Essex. The family-owned institution can trace its roots back to 1914. Owners Chubby and Bessie Woodman are widely credited with inventing the fried clam two years later, after a local fisherman suggested dipping soft-shell clams in evaporated milk, corn flour, and flour before frying them. More than a century later, visitors still line up for this seafood shack's whole-belly fried clams, along with classic lobster rolls, steamers, and chowder. MICHIGAN: Bortell's Fisheries in Ludington Bortell's Fisheries. Robert V./Yelp Bortell's Fisheries has been a fixture on the shores of Lake Michigan since 1898, making it one of the oldest family-owned fish markets and seafood shacks in the state. For more than a century, the Bortell family has smoked and sold locally caught whitefish, trout, salmon, and perch in their market, but the spot is also well known for its smoked fish, fish sandwiches, and fried seafood baskets. MINNESOTA: Smack Shack in Minneapolis Smack Shack. Hli M./Yelp Smack Shack opened as a food truck in 2010 and has since grown into one of Minnesota's most famous seafood destinations. The casual spot built its reputation on buttery Connecticut-style lobster rolls, fresh oysters, shrimp and grits, and seafood boils that have brought a taste of the coast to Minneapolis. Even after expanding into a full-service restaurant, it has held on to its casual, seafood-shack spirit and was featured on "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives" in 2012. MISSISSIPPI: Bozo's Seafood Market in Pascagoula Bozo's Deli And Market. John F./Yelp Bozo's Seafood Market has been a Mississippi Gulf Coast institution since the mid-1950s, serving as both a seafood market and a casual eatery for generations. The family-owned business is famous for its massive po'boys stuffed with fried Gulf shrimp, oysters, and crab, as well as fresh seafood sourced from local waters. MISSOURI: Peacemaker Lobster & Crab in St. Louis Peacemaker Lobster and Crab. Jeremy C./Yelp Peacemaker Lobster and Crab is celebrated for its lobster rolls, oyster po'boys, fresh-shucked oysters, and seasonal seafood boils. Despite being hundreds of miles from the ocean, the restaurant's dedication to sourcing high-quality seafood has earned it a reputation as one of the Midwest's top seafood restaurants, thanks to its James Beard Award-winning chef and owner, Kevin Nashan. MONTANA: Feast Raw Bar & Bistro in Bozeman Feast Raw Bar & Bistro. Alexis M./Yelp Feast Raw Bar & Bistro has redefined seafood dining in Montana by flying in pristine oysters, shellfish, and fresh fish several times a week. More upscale than your typical shack, this restaurant combines Montana's flair for steakhouses with a seafood focus, making it a can't-miss destination. NEBRASKA: Shucks Fish House & Oyster Bar in Omaha Shucks Fish House & Oyster Bar. Malcolm C./Yelp Since opening in 2006, Shucks Fish House & Oyster Bar has become Nebraska's go-to destination for fresh seafood. The casual neighborhood restaurant is famous for its happy-hour oysters, calamari, and other seafood shack favorites. NEVADA: Ocean Seafood Boil in Las Vegas Ocean Seafood Boil. Ocean Seafood Boil/Yelp Las Vegas may be known for celebrity-chef restaurants , but Ocean Seafood Boil has built its reputation the old-fashioned way: generous portions and boldly seasoned seafood. Its casual atmosphere and consistently popular seafood boils have made it one of Nevada's favorite seafood shacks, away from the Strip's typical fine-dining scene. NEW HAMPSHIRE: Brown's Lobster Pound in Seabrook Brown's Seabrook Lobster Pound. Kimberly T./Yelp A New Hampshire summer isn't complete without a visit to Brown's Lobster Pound. Overlooking the salt marshes of Seabrook since 1950, this cash-only seasonal institution serves steamed whole lobsters, lobster rolls, fried seafood platters, and chowder in a relaxed waterfront setting. NEW JERSEY: The Lobster House in Cape May The Lobster House. Theodore H./Yelp The Lobster House has been welcoming diners to Cape May's harbor for decades, becoming one of the Jersey Shore's most recognizable seafood restaurants. Supplied by its own fleet of commercial fishing boats, the restaurant's signature dishes include lobster tails, crab cakes, clams casino, and fresh local catches, making it a fixture of South Jersey dining. NEW MEXICO: Mariscos La Playa in Albuquerque Mariscos La Playa. Mariscos La Playa/Yelp Mariscos La Playa has become New Mexico's seafood standout by merging Mexican cooking styles with Southwestern favorites like towering seafood cocktails, aguachiles, ceviches, grilled fish, and shrimp dishes. It's no shack, but its laidback atmosphere is sure to make you feel right at home. NEW YORK: LUNCH Lobster Roll in Amagansett LUNCH Lobster Roll. Tu-Quyen P./Yelp Better known simply as "Lunch," this local landmark has been slinging up seafood since 1965 and helped cement the lobster roll as a Hamptons summertime icon. Located along Montauk Highway, the casual roadside restaurant has attracted everyone from surfers to celebrities seeking its famous lobster roll, clam chowder, fried clams, and seafood platters. NORTH CAROLINA: Waterfront Seafood Shack in Calabash Waterfront Seafood Shack. Kevin C./Yelp Located in the self-proclaimed "Seafood Capital of the World," Waterfront Seafood Shack celebrates the lightly battered, fried seafood style that made the small fishing town of Calabash famous. The family-owned restaurant, which overlooks the Calabash River, serves local shrimp, oysters, flounder, and scallops, offering visitors an authentic taste of North Carolina seafood. NORTH DAKOTA: Beer And Fish Company in Fargo Beer & Fish Company. Beer & Fish Company/Yelp Beer And Fish Company in downtown Fargo may be relatively new to the city's dining scene — it opened in 2019 — but its seafood favorites keep customers coming back for more. Known for its oysters, mix-and-match fish-and-chip platters, sandwiches, and grilled seafood, this casual eatery has earned praise for bringing coastal-quality seafood to the northern Plains. OHIO: Jolly Roger Seafood House in Port Clinton Jolly Roger Seafood House. Carrie A./Yelp Serving diners on the shores of Lake Erie since 1980, Jolly Roger Seafood House has long been a favorite for its fresh Lake Erie walleye, shrimp, and crab legs. The seafood at this Great Lakes seafood destination often draws long lines of hungry locals and visitors. OKLAHOMA: Bayou Jaq's Seafood Shack in Edmond Bayou Jaq's Seafood Shack. Jon H./Yelp Bayou Jaq's brings the flavors of coastal Louisiana to central Oklahoma with a menu built around crawfish boils, shrimp, crab legs, po'boys, gumbo, and jambalaya. The casual eatery has developed a devoted following for its Cajun-inspired seafood and lively atmosphere, making it one of Oklahoma's best-known seafood restaurants. OREGON: Bowpicker Fish & Chips in Astoria Bowpicker Fish & Chips. Michelle N./Yelp Housed inside a converted gillnet fishing boat, Bowpicker Fish & Chips is one of Oregon's most distinctive seafood shacks. Located across from the Columbia River Maritime Museum, the restaurant's menu focuses on classic fried fish and chips — in this case, beer-battered Albacore tuna and steak fries. PENNSYLVANIA: Mr. Bill's Fresh Seafood in Lancaster Mr Bill's Fresh Seafood. Doug B./Yelp Open since 1973, Mr. Bill's has long been a destination for Pennsylvanians looking for blue crab year-round. Part seafood market and part casual restaurant, the restaurant is also known for its lobster rolls, crab cakes, steamed shrimp, oysters, and daily fresh fish specials. RHODE ISLAND: Roy Boy's Clam Shack in North Kingstown Roy Boy's Clam Shack. Terry B./Yelp Roy Boy's Clam Shack has quickly become one of Rhode Island's standout seafood destinations and was voted by readers of the Providence Journal as the best clam shack in the state. Opened in 2018 by chef and restaurateur Ben Lloyd, the seasonal shack has earned widespread acclaim for its lobster rolls, crispy whole-belly fried clams, clam cakes, chowder, and inventive seafood specials. SOUTH CAROLINA: Bowens Island Restaurant in Charleston Bowen's Island Restaurant. Eugenia M./Yelp Since opening in 1946, Bowens Island Restaurant has been synonymous with low-country seafood, drawing generations of diners for local oysters, shrimp, crab cakes, and sweeping marsh views outside Charleston. In 2006, the family-owned institution was honored with a James Beard Award, recognizing its enduring place in Southern food culture. Despite a fire that destroyed the original restaurant, Bowens has been rebuilt and remains one of the most iconic seafood restaurants in the South. SOUTH DAKOTA: Swamp Daddy's Cajun Kitchen in Sioux Falls Swamp Daddy's Cajun Kitchen. Garrett Z./Yelp Swamp Daddy's Cajun Kitchen has become South Dakota's go-to spot for Gulf Coast flavors, serving crawfish, shrimp boils, po'boys, jambalaya, gumbo, and blackened seafood. The family-owned restaurant has built a loyal following by bringing authentic Louisiana cooking to the northern Plains, making it one of the state's best-known seafood destinations. TENNESSEE: Krustaceans Seafood in Nashville Krustaceans Seafood. Veronica H./Yelp Krustaceans Seafood has become a Nashville favorite thanks to its generously portioned Cajun-style seafood boils featuring shrimp, crab legs, crawfish, lobster tails, and signature house sauces. With plenty of cocktail options to keep the night going, this seafood boil place is a popular spot in Nashville to load up on seafood. TEXAS: Katie's Seafood House in Galveston Katie's Seafood House. Stanley S./Yelp Opened in 2019 by the family behind Katie's Seafood Market, which opened nearly two decades before, the waterfront restaurant serves seafood caught by its own fleet of Gulf fishing boats, ensuring exceptional freshness. Guests come for grilled Gulf snapper, redfish, shrimp, oysters, and seasonal catches while overlooking the working harbor, making it one of the state's most authentic seafood destinations. UTAH: Freshie's Lobster Co. in Salt Lake City Freshies Lobster. Roob D./Yelp Freshie's Lobster Co. has built a cult following by flying in fresh Maine lobster to build its classic New England-style rolls in Utah. Famous for its overflowing lobster rolls, lobster bisque, and lobster mac and cheese, this casual seafood shack has brought classic East Coast flavors and techniques to the West. VERMONT: Ray's Seafood Market & Restaurant in Essex Junction Ray's Seafood Market & Restaurant. Jody W./Yelp Since opening in 1951, Ray's Seafood Market & Restaurant has served Vermonters fresh seafood through its seafood market and adjoining casual restaurant. Known for lobster rolls, fried seafood platters, oysters, and fresh fish flown in several times a week, Ray's has become the state's longtime local favorite. VIRGINIA: Margie & Ray's Crabhouse and Restaurant in Virginia Beach Margie & Ray's Crabhouse. Lynn A./Yelp Margie & Ray's has been serving Chesapeake Bay seafood since the 1960s, earning a reputation as one of coastal Virginia's classic crab houses. The restaurant is best known for its steamed shrimp, she-crab soup, fried seafood platters, and fresh local fish. WASHINGTON: Little Chinook's in Seattle Little Chinooks. Cat P./Yelp Located in Seattle's historic Fishermen's Terminal, Little Chinook's offers one of the city's most authentic waterfront seafood experiences. This counter-service restaurant specializes in wild salmon, halibut, Dungeness crab, fish and chips, and chowder, and overlooks a working commercial fishing harbor. WEST VIRGINIA: Coleman's Fish Market in Wheeling Coleman's Fish Market. Nicole S./Yelp Coleman's Fish Market has been a Wheeling landmark since 1914 and is best known for its fish sandwich, which features a massive piece of fried cod that extends well beyond two pieces of white bread. It was founded by local businessman John Coleman, who initially sold live chickens and eggs before shifting his focus to selling seafood. It's now regarded as one of the best and oldest restaurants in the state. WISCONSIN: Barnacle Bud's in Milwaukee Barnacle Bud's. Jenna K./Yelp Tucked away along Milwaukee's riverfront, Barnacle Bud's has become one of Wisconsin's most beloved hidden gems and has been voted the best waterfront restaurant in the city. The seasonal, open-air seafood shack serves fish sandwiches, shrimp, lobster rolls, fish tacos, and tropical cocktails in a laid-back marina setting that feels worlds away from the buzz of downtown. WYOMING: Rocky Mountain Seafood in Afton Rocky Mountain Seafood. Marie S./Yelp Rocky Mountain Seafood has earned a loyal following by bringing fresh seafood to one of the country's least likely destinations. The family-owned restaurant specializes in seafood favorites like fish and chips, fried seafood platters, and fish tacos, as well as more elevated options like lobster and seared ahi tuna. ARKANSAS: The Oyster Bar in Little Rock
The Oyster Bar.

Carmen S./Yelp

The Oyster Bar has been serving Little Rock since 1975, making it one of Arkansas' longest-running seafood restaurants.

While its atmosphere is a bit more elevated than a traditional seafood shack, its honest, simple cooking and decades-long run have cemented it as a Little Rock institution and earned it a spot on this list.

CALIFORNIA: Neptune's Net in Malibu
Neptune's Net.

Sam M./Yelp

Neptune's Net has been perched along the Pacific Coast Highway since the 1950s, and it has even appeared in major Hollywood films like "The Fast and the Furious."

Diners come for fried seafood, clam chowder, fish and chips, sandwiches, and fish tacos while soaking up sweeping ocean views that have made Neptune's Net one of the state's most recognizable seafood stops.

COLORADO: Big Mac and Little Lu's Seafood Restaurant in Westminster
Big Mac & Little Lu's Seafood Restaurant.

Bonni R./Yelp

In a state better known for steaks than seafood, Big Mac & Little Lu's has become a Colorado favorite by flying in fresh seafood several times a week.

Open since 2013, the restaurant has built a devoted following for its fresh New England-style lobster rolls, crispy crab cakes, clam chowder, and classic fish and chips.

The restaurant's longevity and reputation for fresh seafood in landlocked Colorado have made it a standout seafood spot.

CONNECTICUT: Abbott's Lobster in the Rough in Noank
Abbott's Lobster In the Rough.

Ian L./Yelp

For generations, Abbott's Lobster in the Rough has defined the classic New England seafood shack experience.

Operating seasonally on the Mystic River since 1947, it serves up an overflowing hot Connecticut lobster roll, packed with warm lobster meat and served with drawn butter, but it also offers Maine versions dressed with mayonnaise.

Picnic tables overlooking the water, steamed clams, chowder, and a rich maritime history have made going to Abbott's one of Connecticut's most beloved summer traditions.

DELAWARE: JR's Seafood Shack in Fenwick Island
JR's Seafood Shack.

Josh T./Yelp

Just steps from the Delaware-Maryland line, JR's Seafood Shack has earned a loyal following by serving fresh local seafood without the fuss of a high-end restaurant, but a bit more elevated than the typical roadside seafood shack.

The casual roadside stop is known for calamari, crab dip, steamed seafood, and low-country boils, making it a favorite stop for beachgoers headed to Fenwick Island.

FLORIDA: Star Fish Company in Cortez
Star Fish Co Seafood Market and Restaurant.

Kaitlyn S./Yelp

Star Fish Company feels like a glimpse into Old Florida. Operating as both a seafood market and a dockside restaurant in the historic fishing village of Cortez, the family-owned business serves whatever fresh catches local fishermen happen to bring in that day.

Popular items include fresh grouper, fried fish, and Gulf shrimp, and its connection to the local fishing communities makes it one of the most authentic seafood shacks in the state.

GEORGIA: The Crab Shack on Tybee Island
The Crab Shack.

Ray L./Yelp

Billing itself as "where the elite eat in their bare feet," The Crab Shack has become one of Georgia's most iconic seafood destinations thanks to its sprawling waterfront setting and famously messy seafood boils.

The quirky atmosphere — complete with wandering cats, alligators, and marsh views — has made it a must-visit for decades.

HAWAII: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku
Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Oahu.

Steven C./Yelp

Few food trucks have achieved the legendary status of Giovanni's Shrimp Truck. What started as a humble roadside stand has since become a Hawaiian icon.

Parked on O'ahu's North Shore since the early 1990s, the graffiti-covered truck helped popularize Hawaii's famous shrimp plate and now draws visitors from around the world for its buttery garlic shrimp over rice.

It has two North Shore locations: the original location in Kahuku and a second, beloved spot in Hale'iwa.

IDAHO: Fresh Off the Hook in Boise
Fresh Off The Hook.

Joe C./Yelp

Fresh Off the Hook has spent decades proving Idaho can do excellent seafood despite being hundreds of miles from the coast.

The family-owned restaurant flies in fresh seafood several times a week and serves everything from cedar plank salmon and ahi tuna to fish tacos and oysters.

ILLINOIS: Calumet Fisheries in Chicago
Calumet Fisheries.

Izzy L./Yelp

Few seafood shacks are as legendary as Calumet Fisheries, a James Beard award-winning restaurant that has been smoking fish over oak fires since 1948, though the original site and smokehouse date back 20 years earlier.

Located beside the Calumet River on Chicago's Southeast Side, the no-frills smokehouse is famous for fried seafood as well as smoked shrimp, salmon, trout, and pepper-and-garlic smoked fish.

INDIANA: Caplinger's Fresh Catch in Indianapolis
Caplinger's Fresh Catch.

Caplinger's Fresh Catch/Yelp

Part seafood market, part casual restaurant, Caplinger's Fresh Catch has become Indiana's go-to destination for high-quality seafood.

The family-owned business is known for lobster rolls, crab cakes, oysters, po'boys, and Seafood Philly, a mashup between a Philly cheesesteak and a lobster roll.

IOWA: Waterfront Seafood Market in West Des Moines
Waterfront Seafood Market.

Todd B./Yelp

Waterfront Seafood Market has served Iowans fresh seafood for more than 40 years, earning a reputation as the state's premier fish market and casual seafood restaurant.

Diners come from far and wide to try the market's fresh sushi, peel-and-eat shrimp, fried seafood baskets, and crab cakes.

KANSAS: Jarocho in Kansas City
Jarocho.

Chris L./Yelp

Jarocho has earned national acclaim by bringing the flavors of Mexico's Veracruz coast to the Kansas City area.

More polished than a traditional shack, its focus on high-quality seafood has made it a standout spot in the landlocked state.

KENTUCKY: Mike Linnig's Famous Seafood Restaurant in Louisville
Mike Linnig's Restaurant.

Kelly J./Yelp

Mike Linnig's has welcomed diners since the 1920s, making it one of Kentucky's oldest seafood restaurants.

The sprawling outdoor beer garden and family-friendly atmosphere are as much a draw as the generous platters of classic Southern favorites like fried fish, frog legs, fried oysters, and peel-and-eat shrimp.

LOUISIANA: Middendorf's in Manchac
Middendorf's.

Middendorf's/Yelp

Open since 1934, Middendorf's has been one of Louisiana's oldest and most defining seafood restaurants, particularly famous for its thin-fried catfish.

Though not a traditional shack, it serves up many of the classic items you'd expect to find in the bayou, from seafood gumbo to crawfish étouffée and fried shrimp.

MAINE: The Clam Shack in Kennebunkport
The Clam Shack.

Rob M./Yelp

The Clam Shack has been drawing summer crowds since 1968 with what many argue is one of the country's greatest lobster rolls, and a hallmark of Maine seafood.

However, visitors might be surprised to learn that the Clam Shack doesn't specialize in Maine-style rolls. Unlike most versions, its roll features claw, knuckle, and tail meat lightly dressed with butter or mayonnaise and served on a round, locally baked bun.

Along with whole-belly fried clams and waterfront views in Kennebunkport, it's become one of Maine's most celebrated seafood shacks.

MARYLAND: The Crab Claw in St. Michaels
The Crab Claw.

Soojin J./Yelp

The Crab Claw has overlooked St. Michaels Harbor since its opening in 1965, and is one of the Chesapeake Bay's most enduring crab houses.

The restaurant has built its reputation on its famous steamed Maryland blue crabs coated in seasoning, along with classic crab cakes, oysters, soft-shell crabs, and cream of crab soup served in a casual atmosphere.

MASSACHUSETTS: Woodman's of Essex in Essex
Woodman's of Essex.

Huy P./Yelp

Few seafood shacks are as famous as Woodman's of Essex.

The family-owned institution can trace its roots back to 1914. Owners Chubby and Bessie Woodman are widely credited with inventing the fried clam two years later, after a local fisherman suggested dipping soft-shell clams in evaporated milk, corn flour, and flour before frying them.

More than a century later, visitors still line up for this seafood shack's whole-belly fried clams, along with classic lobster rolls, steamers, and chowder.

MICHIGAN: Bortell's Fisheries in Ludington
Bortell's Fisheries.

Robert V./Yelp

Bortell's Fisheries has been a fixture on the shores of Lake Michigan since 1898, making it one of the oldest family-owned fish markets and seafood shacks in the state.

For more than a century, the Bortell family has smoked and sold locally caught whitefish, trout, salmon, and perch in their market, but the spot is also well known for its smoked fish, fish sandwiches, and fried seafood baskets.

MINNESOTA: Smack Shack in Minneapolis
Smack Shack.

Hli M./Yelp

Smack Shack opened as a food truck in 2010 and has since grown into one of Minnesota's most famous seafood destinations.

The casual spot built its reputation on buttery Connecticut-style lobster rolls, fresh oysters, shrimp and grits, and seafood boils that have brought a taste of the coast to Minneapolis.

Even after expanding into a full-service restaurant, it has held on to its casual, seafood-shack spirit and was featured on "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives" in 2012.

MISSISSIPPI: Bozo's Seafood Market in Pascagoula
Bozo's Deli And Market.

John F./Yelp

Bozo's Seafood Market has been a Mississippi Gulf Coast institution since the mid-1950s, serving as both a seafood market and a casual eatery for generations.

The family-owned business is famous for its massive po'boys stuffed with fried Gulf shrimp, oysters, and crab, as well as fresh seafood sourced from local waters.

MISSOURI: Peacemaker Lobster & Crab in St. Louis
Peacemaker Lobster and Crab.

Jeremy C./Yelp

Peacemaker Lobster and Crab is celebrated for its lobster rolls, oyster po'boys, fresh-shucked oysters, and seasonal seafood boils.

Despite being hundreds of miles from the ocean, the restaurant's dedication to sourcing high-quality seafood has earned it a reputation as one of the Midwest's top seafood restaurants, thanks to its James Beard Award-winning chef and owner, Kevin Nashan.

MONTANA: Feast Raw Bar & Bistro in Bozeman
Feast Raw Bar & Bistro.

Alexis M./Yelp

Feast Raw Bar & Bistro has redefined seafood dining in Montana by flying in pristine oysters, shellfish, and fresh fish several times a week.

More upscale than your typical shack, this restaurant combines Montana's flair for steakhouses with a seafood focus, making it a can't-miss destination.

NEBRASKA: Shucks Fish House & Oyster Bar in Omaha
Shucks Fish House & Oyster Bar.

Malcolm C./Yelp

Since opening in 2006, Shucks Fish House & Oyster Bar has become Nebraska's go-to destination for fresh seafood.

The casual neighborhood restaurant is famous for its happy-hour oysters, calamari, and other seafood shack favorites.

NEVADA: Ocean Seafood Boil in Las Vegas
Ocean Seafood Boil.

Ocean Seafood Boil/Yelp

Las Vegas may be known for celebrity-chef restaurants, but Ocean Seafood Boil has built its reputation the old-fashioned way: generous portions and boldly seasoned seafood.

Its casual atmosphere and consistently popular seafood boils have made it one of Nevada's favorite seafood shacks, away from the Strip's typical fine-dining scene.

NEW HAMPSHIRE: Brown's Lobster Pound in Seabrook
Brown's Seabrook Lobster Pound.

Kimberly T./Yelp

A New Hampshire summer isn't complete without a visit to Brown's Lobster Pound.

Overlooking the salt marshes of Seabrook since 1950, this cash-only seasonal institution serves steamed whole lobsters, lobster rolls, fried seafood platters, and chowder in a relaxed waterfront setting.

NEW JERSEY: The Lobster House in Cape May
The Lobster House.

Theodore H./Yelp

The Lobster House has been welcoming diners to Cape May's harbor for decades, becoming one of the Jersey Shore's most recognizable seafood restaurants.

Supplied by its own fleet of commercial fishing boats, the restaurant's signature dishes include lobster tails, crab cakes, clams casino, and fresh local catches, making it a fixture of South Jersey dining.

NEW MEXICO: Mariscos La Playa in Albuquerque
Mariscos La Playa.

Mariscos La Playa/Yelp

Mariscos La Playa has become New Mexico's seafood standout by merging Mexican cooking styles with Southwestern favorites like towering seafood cocktails, aguachiles, ceviches, grilled fish, and shrimp dishes.

It's no shack, but its laidback atmosphere is sure to make you feel right at home.

NEW YORK: LUNCH Lobster Roll in Amagansett
LUNCH Lobster Roll.

Tu-Quyen P./Yelp

Better known simply as "Lunch," this local landmark has been slinging up seafood since 1965 and helped cement the lobster roll as a Hamptons summertime icon.

Located along Montauk Highway, the casual roadside restaurant has attracted everyone from surfers to celebrities seeking its famous lobster roll, clam chowder, fried clams, and seafood platters.

NORTH CAROLINA: Waterfront Seafood Shack in Calabash
Waterfront Seafood Shack.

Kevin C./Yelp

Located in the self-proclaimed "Seafood Capital of the World," Waterfront Seafood Shack celebrates the lightly battered, fried seafood style that made the small fishing town of Calabash famous.

The family-owned restaurant, which overlooks the Calabash River, serves local shrimp, oysters, flounder, and scallops, offering visitors an authentic taste of North Carolina seafood.

NORTH DAKOTA: Beer And Fish Company in Fargo
Beer & Fish Company.

Beer & Fish Company/Yelp

Beer And Fish Company in downtown Fargo may be relatively new to the city's dining scene — it opened in 2019 — but its seafood favorites keep customers coming back for more.

Known for its oysters, mix-and-match fish-and-chip platters, sandwiches, and grilled seafood, this casual eatery has earned praise for bringing coastal-quality seafood to the northern Plains.

OHIO: Jolly Roger Seafood House in Port Clinton
Jolly Roger Seafood House.

Carrie A./Yelp

Serving diners on the shores of Lake Erie since 1980, Jolly Roger Seafood House has long been a favorite for its fresh Lake Erie walleye, shrimp, and crab legs.

The seafood at this Great Lakes seafood destination often draws long lines of hungry locals and visitors.

OKLAHOMA: Bayou Jaq's Seafood Shack in Edmond
Bayou Jaq's Seafood Shack.

Jon H./Yelp

Bayou Jaq's brings the flavors of coastal Louisiana to central Oklahoma with a menu built around crawfish boils, shrimp, crab legs, po'boys, gumbo, and jambalaya.

The casual eatery has developed a devoted following for its Cajun-inspired seafood and lively atmosphere, making it one of Oklahoma's best-known seafood restaurants.

OREGON: Bowpicker Fish & Chips in Astoria
Bowpicker Fish & Chips.

Michelle N./Yelp

Housed inside a converted gillnet fishing boat, Bowpicker Fish & Chips is one of Oregon's most distinctive seafood shacks.

Located across from the Columbia River Maritime Museum, the restaurant's menu focuses on classic fried fish and chips — in this case, beer-battered Albacore tuna and steak fries.

PENNSYLVANIA: Mr. Bill's Fresh Seafood in Lancaster
Mr Bill's Fresh Seafood.

Doug B./Yelp

Open since 1973, Mr. Bill's has long been a destination for Pennsylvanians looking for blue crab year-round.

Part seafood market and part casual restaurant, the restaurant is also known for its lobster rolls, crab cakes, steamed shrimp, oysters, and daily fresh fish specials.

RHODE ISLAND: Roy Boy's Clam Shack in North Kingstown
Roy Boy's Clam Shack.

Terry B./Yelp

Roy Boy's Clam Shack has quickly become one of Rhode Island's standout seafood destinations and was voted by readers of the Providence Journal as the best clam shack in the state.

Opened in 2018 by chef and restaurateur Ben Lloyd, the seasonal shack has earned widespread acclaim for its lobster rolls, crispy whole-belly fried clams, clam cakes, chowder, and inventive seafood specials.

SOUTH CAROLINA: Bowens Island Restaurant in Charleston
Bowen's Island Restaurant.

Eugenia M./Yelp

Since opening in 1946, Bowens Island Restaurant has been synonymous with low-country seafood, drawing generations of diners for local oysters, shrimp, crab cakes, and sweeping marsh views outside Charleston.

In 2006, the family-owned institution was honored with a James Beard Award, recognizing its enduring place in Southern food culture. Despite a fire that destroyed the original restaurant, Bowens has been rebuilt and remains one of the most iconic seafood restaurants in the South.

SOUTH DAKOTA: Swamp Daddy's Cajun Kitchen in Sioux Falls
Swamp Daddy's Cajun Kitchen.

Garrett Z./Yelp

Swamp Daddy's Cajun Kitchen has become South Dakota's go-to spot for Gulf Coast flavors, serving crawfish, shrimp boils, po'boys, jambalaya, gumbo, and blackened seafood.

The family-owned restaurant has built a loyal following by bringing authentic Louisiana cooking to the northern Plains, making it one of the state's best-known seafood destinations.

TENNESSEE: Krustaceans Seafood in Nashville
Krustaceans Seafood.

Veronica H./Yelp

Krustaceans Seafood has become a Nashville favorite thanks to its generously portioned Cajun-style seafood boils featuring shrimp, crab legs, crawfish, lobster tails, and signature house sauces.

With plenty of cocktail options to keep the night going, this seafood boil place is a popular spot in Nashville to load up on seafood.

TEXAS: Katie's Seafood House in Galveston
Katie's Seafood House.

Stanley S./Yelp

Opened in 2019 by the family behind Katie's Seafood Market, which opened nearly two decades before, the waterfront restaurant serves seafood caught by its own fleet of Gulf fishing boats, ensuring exceptional freshness.

Guests come for grilled Gulf snapper, redfish, shrimp, oysters, and seasonal catches while overlooking the working harbor, making it one of the state's most authentic seafood destinations.

UTAH: Freshie's Lobster Co. in Salt Lake City
Freshies Lobster.

Roob D./Yelp

Freshie's Lobster Co. has built a cult following by flying in fresh Maine lobster to build its classic New England-style rolls in Utah.

Famous for its overflowing lobster rolls, lobster bisque, and lobster mac and cheese, this casual seafood shack has brought classic East Coast flavors and techniques to the West.

VERMONT: Ray's Seafood Market & Restaurant in Essex Junction
Ray's Seafood Market & Restaurant.

Jody W./Yelp

Since opening in 1951, Ray's Seafood Market & Restaurant has served Vermonters fresh seafood through its seafood market and adjoining casual restaurant.

Known for lobster rolls, fried seafood platters, oysters, and fresh fish flown in several times a week, Ray's has become the state's longtime local favorite.

VIRGINIA: Margie & Ray's Crabhouse and Restaurant in Virginia Beach
Margie & Ray's Crabhouse.

Lynn A./Yelp

Margie & Ray's has been serving Chesapeake Bay seafood since the 1960s, earning a reputation as one of coastal Virginia's classic crab houses.

The restaurant is best known for its steamed shrimp, she-crab soup, fried seafood platters, and fresh local fish.

WASHINGTON: Little Chinook's in Seattle
Little Chinooks.

Cat P./Yelp

Located in Seattle's historic Fishermen's Terminal, Little Chinook's offers one of the city's most authentic waterfront seafood experiences.

This counter-service restaurant specializes in wild salmon, halibut, Dungeness crab, fish and chips, and chowder, and overlooks a working commercial fishing harbor.

WEST VIRGINIA: Coleman's Fish Market in Wheeling
Coleman's Fish Market.

Nicole S./Yelp

Coleman's Fish Market has been a Wheeling landmark since 1914 and is best known for its fish sandwich, which features a massive piece of fried cod that extends well beyond two pieces of white bread.

It was founded by local businessman John Coleman, who initially sold live chickens and eggs before shifting his focus to selling seafood. It's now regarded as one of the best and oldest restaurants in the state.

WISCONSIN: Barnacle Bud's in Milwaukee
Barnacle Bud's.

Jenna K./Yelp

Tucked away along Milwaukee's riverfront, Barnacle Bud's has become one of Wisconsin's most beloved hidden gems and has been voted the best waterfront restaurant in the city.

The seasonal, open-air seafood shack serves fish sandwiches, shrimp, lobster rolls, fish tacos, and tropical cocktails in a laid-back marina setting that feels worlds away from the buzz of downtown.

WYOMING: Rocky Mountain Seafood in Afton
Rocky Mountain Seafood.

Marie S./Yelp

Rocky Mountain Seafood has earned a loyal following by bringing fresh seafood to one of the country's least likely destinations.

The family-owned restaurant specializes in seafood favorites like fish and chips, fried seafood platters, and fish tacos, as well as more elevated options like lobster and seared ahi tuna.

items.title: X wants to keep suing advertisers, asks 5th Circuit to overrule district judge
items.summary: Elon Musk's X is trying to revive a lawsuit against advertisers it's accusing of illegally boycotting the social media platform, despite previously reaching a settlement to end litigation against an ad-industry trade group. "This case involves an unusually brazen group boycott," X said in a filing yesterday. "That misconduct has drawn the attention of regulators and Congress. There is no valid reason that this effort by the direct victim to recover its massive economic losses from that boycott should not move forward." X's lawsuit was thrown out in March when US District Judge Jane Boyle in the Northern District of Texas ruled that advertisers did not commit any antitrust violation. Last week, Musk reached a settlement with the World Federation of Advertisers, the first defendant named in the lawsuit. Read full article Comments

items.title: Thousands of server motherboards are vulnerable to controller flaws that could give attackers hardware-level control
items.summary: Baseboard management controllers, or BMCs, are small computers built into nearly every enterprise server. They have their own firmware, operating system, network stack, and IP address. Administrators use them to reboot machines, install updates, reinstall operating systems, and monitor hardware, even when the main server is powered off or unresponsive. Read Entire Article

items.title: Jealously Watching OpenAI and Anthropic, Meta Suddenly Claims That Its AI Went on a Hacking Spree Too
items.summary: Last month, OpenAI revealed that a group of its AI models had broken containment , hacking into the systems of open source AI platform Hugging Face. On one hand, experts saw the incident as the latest warning sign that AI models had gotten to the point of being able to autonomously infiltrate targets, a threat we’ve been aware of for years rapidly turning into a reality. On the other, a more skeptical read of the situation is that OpenAI could have orchestrated the hack as part of a “ publicity stunt ” — or at least lowered its guard just enough to allow it to happen, knowing the publicity would be invaluable. After all, just three months earlier, competitor Anthropic had made major headlines by announcing that its own Mythos AI model had similarly broken containment. Put simply, it’s in the companies’ best interest to paint their AI models as capable enough to pose a real-world threat, especially as the industry grows ever more competitive. Now the situation has gotten even stranger as a third company, Meta, has entered the fray. As the Wall Street Journal reports , the Mark Zuckerberg-led tech giant is claiming that during a recent test of one of its AI model conducted by an independent company, the AI accessed the internet and hacked a third-party service — an narrative that’s starting to get awfully familiar at this point. According to The Information , the model involved was Meta’s Muse Spark 1.1 , the company’s most advanced model yet, which was released by its Superintelligence Labs last month. Per the publication, the model breached an unidentified company’s systems and changed its internal environment. Meta claims a “misconfiguration” during the hacking test had allowed its model to escape. A source told the WSJ that it was the same cybersecurity benchmark test that led to previous hacking incidents at Anthropic and OpenAI. Earlier this week, the company that conducted benchmark tests for all three AI companies, called Irregular, said it had caught OpenAI and Anthropic AI agents gaining unauthorized access to secure systems. As we await more details regarding the latest incident — Meta has promised to investigate and publish a report — the suspicious optics of the situation are hard to escape. Meta has long struggled to keep up with the competition as the AI race continues to heat up. Could the company be looking for favorable media coverage about how its AI model is similarly capable of breaking containment? Irregular said it hadn’t noticed any “current open issues” related to its test environment, per the WSJ . But while there wasn’t any real-world harm — at least that we know of — stemming from these hacks, researchers warn that the threat of AI models going rogue is coming to a head. Just earlier this week, the UK government-backed AI Security Institute revealed that OpenAI and Anthropic models took “unsanctioned action on the live internet” and went as far as to create fake identities on GitHub to pressure a human user into approving a malware-tainted software update. “What they’re doing is coming up with very sophisticated strategies or cyberattacks to be able to achieve the goal that they’ve been given,” global chief AI officer of advertising firm WPP Daniel Hulme told the BBC . “When you give an AI a goal, if you don’t think of all the ways it might be able to achieve the goal, it will find a way to achieve a goal that you haven’t thought about.” More on the hacks: OpenAI’s Escaped Models Were Allegedly Rampaging More Extensively Than Previously Reported The post Jealously Watching OpenAI and Anthropic, Meta Suddenly Claims That Its AI Went on a Hacking Spree Too appeared first on Futurism .
items.summary_html:
Last month, OpenAI revealed that a group of its AI models had broken containment, hacking into the systems of open source AI platform Hugging Face.

On one hand, experts saw the incident as the latest warning sign that AI models had gotten to the point of being able to autonomously infiltrate targets, a threat we’ve been aware of for years rapidly turning into a reality.

On the other, a more skeptical read of the situation is that OpenAI could have orchestrated the hack as part of a “publicity stunt” — or at least lowered its guard just enough to allow it to happen, knowing the publicity would be invaluable. After all, just three months earlier, competitor Anthropic had made major headlines by announcing that its own Mythos AI model had similarly broken containment.

Put simply, it’s in the companies’ best interest to paint their AI models as capable enough to pose a real-world threat, especially as the industry grows ever more competitive.

Now the situation has gotten even stranger as a third company, Meta, has entered the fray. As the Wall Street Journal reports, the Mark Zuckerberg-led tech giant is claiming that during a recent test of one of its AI model conducted by an independent company, the AI accessed the internet and hacked a third-party service — an narrative that’s starting to get awfully familiar at this point.

According to The Information, the model involved was Meta’s Muse Spark 1.1, the company’s most advanced model yet, which was released by its Superintelligence Labs last month. Per the publication, the model breached an unidentified company’s systems and changed its internal environment.

Meta claims a “misconfiguration” during the hacking test had allowed its model to escape. A source told the WSJ that it was the same cybersecurity benchmark test that led to previous hacking incidents at Anthropic and OpenAI. Earlier this week, the company that conducted benchmark tests for all three AI companies, called Irregular, said it had caught OpenAI and Anthropic AI agents gaining unauthorized access to secure systems.

As we await more details regarding the latest incident — Meta has promised to investigate and publish a report — the suspicious optics of the situation are hard to escape. Meta has long struggled to keep up with the competition as the AI race continues to heat up. Could the company be looking for favorable media coverage about how its AI model is similarly capable of breaking containment?

Irregular said it hadn’t noticed any “current open issues” related to its test environment, per the WSJ. But while there wasn’t any real-world harm — at least that we know of — stemming from these hacks, researchers warn that the threat of AI models going rogue is coming to a head.

Just earlier this week, the UK government-backed AI Security Institute revealed that OpenAI and Anthropic models took “unsanctioned action on the live internet” and went as far as to create fake identities on GitHub to pressure a human user into approving a malware-tainted software update.

“What they’re doing is coming up with very sophisticated strategies or cyberattacks to be able to achieve the goal that they’ve been given,” global chief AI officer of advertising firm WPP Daniel Hulme told the BBC. “When you give an AI a goal, if you don’t think of all the ways it might be able to achieve the goal, it will find a way to achieve a goal that you haven’t thought about.”

More on the hacks: OpenAI’s Escaped Models Were Allegedly Rampaging More Extensively Than Previously Reported

The post Jealously Watching OpenAI and Anthropic, Meta Suddenly Claims That Its AI Went on a Hacking Spree Too appeared first on Futurism.

items.title: Suno hopes to go legit with watermarks for AI-generated music
items.summary: The Internet is awash in AI content, and it's not always easy to tell it apart from genuine human creations. While images and videos are perhaps the most obvious type of AI slop, streaming music services like Spotify are also being inundated with AI-generated tunes . Suno is one of the most prolific sources of this AI music, but the company now says it's looking to clean up its act with watermarks and policy changes. In a blog post announcing the plans, Suno CEO and co-founder Mikey Shulman says this is a necessary change to meet "emerging industry standards" for the labeling of AI content. Soon, the company will add watermarks to all audio outputs from its models, giving platforms the option to mark content as AI or block it entirely. Shulman doesn't say if Suno will rely on an in-house solution or a ready-made solution like Google's SynthID. Google recently began licensing SynthID to other companies . Google says the tech has been used to label 60,000 years' worth of audio generated by its Gemini models, plus more than 100 billion images and videos. Read full article Comments

items.title: These 3 charts show female-dominated jobs are actually the most exposed to AI
items.summary: Jonathan Brady/PA Images As the impacts of artificial intelligence (AI) sweep across the labour force, it’s understandable for workers to be concerned about which jobs are most at risk of being replaced by technology. Women make up the majority of workers in the care sector where human interactions matter most – child care, nursing and aged care. So, policymakers might reasonably presume that women’s jobs are largely shielded from the impacts of AI. But our analysis of recent data from government agency Jobs and Skills Australia shows that it’s actually female-concentrated segments of the workforce that are most exposed to AI-fuelled automation. Which jobs are most at risk? The agency calculated an “automation exposure score” for every occupation in the workforce, measuring the potential for a worker’s tasks to be done by AI technologies. Clerical and administrative jobs are among those with the highest automation exposure scores. This aligns with economists’ expectations that AI is well suited to alleviate human effort for repetitive routine tasks. Yet this sector, which is highly exposed to automation, is also more than 70% female and provides almost one in five jobs for all women in the Australian workforce. This gender pattern shows up when we look at the 20 top occupations most at risk of automation. 15 of these jobs are female-dominated. Of these, five would be classified as highly female-dominated, comprised of at least 80% women. Secretaries, receptionists, bookkeepers, and accounting, human resources and payroll clerks are all among these top 20 occupations most at risk of being displaced by automation. Only one occupation on this top 20 list is moderately male dominated: financial dealers. The remaining four are gender-balanced. Contrast this to the 20 occupations that are least exposed to automation. Seventeen of these are male-dominated. Female-concentrated jobs make up just three of these jobs most sheltered from being displaced by AI. Is AI already replacing these jobs? A slowdown in job vacancy numbers could signal that these effects of AI are being felt in the economy. Internet job vacancy data , also collected by Jobs and Skills Australia, shows that vacancies for many of these jobs highly exposed to automation have been shrinking over the past three years. And by a larger magnitude than the slowdown across the wider workforce. For instance, vacancies for personal assistants and bookkeepers for the month of June 2026 were around 22% lower than at the same time a year earlier. Openings for general clerks were down by around 9%. By comparison, total workforce vacancies were only around 1.7% weaker. Among the occupations less exposed to AI, vacancies for concreters were up by 5.5%, while electricians were up by 14.3%. At this stage, trades and labourer jobs are less exposed to automation. These hands-on jobs still require human judgement and dexterity to navigate physical conditions that can be unpredictable and differ site by site. Checking for blind spots All kinds of groups – tech companies, governments , education providers and researchers – are trying to predict how AI will disrupt different jobs across the workforce. Our analysis shows that unless we intentionally apply a gender lens, we could end up ignoring gender patterns in AI’s impacts. The federal government already requires all new policy proposals to undergo a gender analysis . This requirement should therefore also apply to policies and decisions by the newly announced Office of AI . In particular, applying a gender lens can inform the design of policies to support the labour market’s adaptation to and adoption of AI. This puts us on the front foot to design smart policies to proactively address AI’s disruption, instead of waiting to respond after the fallout. For instance, having detected the higher risk of these heavily female jobs to AI automation, we can set up systems to recognise the skills of clerical and administrative workers that can be easily transferred, to match them to new opportunities. This could include the new and emerging jobs being created by AI, as well as human-centered jobs and tasks requiring critical judgement that AI can’t replace. Applying this gender lens to Australia’s AI policies will support a dynamic, adaptive labour market hand-in-hand with a gender equitable economy. Leonora Risse receives research funding from the Trawalla Foundation and the Women's Leadership Institute Australia. She serves as an Expert Panel Member for the Fair Work Commission and the Parliamentary Budget Office. She formerly served on the Jobs and Skills Australia Advisory Panel for the Gender Economic Equality Study. Elise Stephenson receives research funding from the Australian Research Council (DE250100718), the Australian Government, and the Women's Leadership Institute of Australia. She is currently supporting the work of the Victorian Women's Trust (VWT) on gendered harms of AI through VWT's Feminist Researcher in Residence program.

But our analysis of recent data from government agency Jobs and Skills Australia shows that it’s actually female-concentrated segments of the workforce that are most exposed to AI-fuelled automation.

Which jobs are most at risk?

The agency calculated an “automation exposure score” for every occupation in the workforce, measuring the potential for a worker’s tasks to be done by AI technologies.

Clerical and administrative jobs are among those with the highest automation exposure scores. This aligns with economists’ expectations that AI is well suited to alleviate human effort for repetitive routine tasks.

Yet this sector, which is highly exposed to automation, is also more than 70% female and provides almost one in five jobs for all women in the Australian workforce.

This gender pattern shows up when we look at the 20 top occupations most at risk of automation. 15 of these jobs are female-dominated. Of these, five would be classified as highly female-dominated, comprised of at least 80% women.

Secretaries, receptionists, bookkeepers, and accounting, human resources and payroll clerks are all among these top 20 occupations most at risk of being displaced by automation.

Only one occupation on this top 20 list is moderately male dominated: financial dealers. The remaining four are gender-balanced.

Contrast this to the 20 occupations that are least exposed to automation. Seventeen of these are male-dominated. Female-concentrated jobs make up just three of these jobs most sheltered from being displaced by AI.

Is AI already replacing these jobs?

A slowdown in job vacancy numbers could signal that these effects of AI are being felt in the economy.

Internet job vacancy data, also collected by Jobs and Skills Australia, shows that vacancies for many of these jobs highly exposed to automation have been shrinking over the past three years. And by a larger magnitude than the slowdown across the wider workforce.

For instance, vacancies for personal assistants and bookkeepers for the month of June 2026 were around 22% lower than at the same time a year earlier. Openings for general clerks were down by around 9%.

By comparison, total workforce vacancies were only around 1.7% weaker.

Among the occupations less exposed to AI, vacancies for concreters were up by 5.5%, while electricians were up by 14.3%.

At this stage, trades and labourer jobs are less exposed to automation. These hands-on jobs still require human judgement and dexterity to navigate physical conditions that can be unpredictable and differ site by site.

Checking for blind spots

All kinds of groups – tech companies, governments, education providers and researchers – are trying to predict how AI will disrupt different jobs across the workforce.

Our analysis shows that unless we intentionally apply a gender lens, we could end up ignoring gender patterns in AI’s impacts.

The federal government already requires all new policy proposals to undergo a gender analysis. This requirement should therefore also apply to policies and decisions by the newly announced Office of AI.

In particular, applying a gender lens can inform the design of policies to support the labour market’s adaptation to and adoption of AI.

This puts us on the front foot to design smart policies to proactively address AI’s disruption, instead of waiting to respond after the fallout.

For instance, having detected the higher risk of these heavily female jobs to AI automation, we can set up systems to recognise the skills of clerical and administrative workers that can be easily transferred, to match them to new opportunities.

This could include the new and emerging jobs being created by AI, as well as human-centered jobs and tasks requiring critical judgement that AI can’t replace.

Applying this gender lens to Australia’s AI policies will support a dynamic, adaptive labour market hand-in-hand with a gender equitable economy.

She serves as an Expert Panel Member for the Fair Work Commission and the Parliamentary Budget Office. She formerly served on the Jobs and Skills Australia Advisory Panel for the Gender Economic Equality Study.

items.title: Cloudflare Introduces Kitesurf: An Agent-First Web Browser That Runs Entirely in V8 Isolates on Cloudflare Workers
items.summary: Cloudflare has released Kitesurf , a stateless web browser built specifically for AI agents. It runs entirely in V8 isolates on Cloudflare Workers , with no Chromium underneath. Browser engines like Chromium were built for humans, and their memory and compute overhead makes one-browser-per-agent prohibitively expensive. Agents do not need tabs, extensions, or pixel-perfect 60-fps rendering. They need machine-readable content, low token overhead, scalability, and isolation against threats like prompt injection. Kitesurf drops the human-facing parts and keeps what models use. It already passes 215,000+ Web Platform Tests and is available now, free while in beta, through Browser Run . Is It Deployable Yes, as a free beta in Browser Run , behind per-account limits . Treat it as production-adjacent: strong for compatible sites and one-shot tasks, with Chromium as the fallback for complex pages. Adoption cost is minimal — existing Puppeteer, Playwright, and MCP clients work by adding a single browser=kitesurf parameter. Company levels: Startups and indie agent builders benefit most from the 3–7× lower CPU and memory footprint. Mid-market SaaS and enterprises already on Cloudflare Workers can switch selected workloads with one parameter. Industries: AI agent platforms, web data extraction, SaaS automation, competitive monitoring, PDF/document generation, and search/RAG ingestion pipelines. Applications: Agent web browsing, screenshots, HTML extraction, PDF rendering, and bursty one-shot Quick Actions . Potential customers: AI engineers building browser-using agents, platform engineers scaling automation fleets, data engineers and data scientists running extraction jobs, and technical founders tracking per-session infrastructure costs. Not yet: Video, WebGL, TLS-fingerprint bot challenges, and long authenticated stateful sessions — keep those on the Chromium default. Architecture: Engine, PageScript, PageRenderer Kitesurf splits the browser into isolated Workers components. The Engine is the only public-facing piece. It speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) over WebSocket plus HTTP REST, and stores each session’s state. Every other component is stateless and disposable. PageScript is built on Dynamic Workers . Each page or out-of-process iframe gets its own long-lived isolate with a clean globalThis and DOM. HTML and CSS parsing use Blitz , a modular Rust rendering engine, and Stylo , Firefox’s CSS parser. Because Workers does not support native eval , occasional eval calls run through Boa JS , a Rust ECMAScript engine, a runtime on top of a runtime. PageRenderer rasterizes the computed scene into JPEG/PNG or PDF using blitz-paint and Parley for text shaping. A dedicated SandboxOutbound worker is the only component allowed to touch the network. It enforces CORS, injects browser-shaped headers, keeps per-page cookie jars, and returns a 403 for anything violating policy. Benchmarks: 3–7× Cheaper, ~1.7–1.8× Slower WPT coverage grows by hundreds of passing tests weekly. On Cloudflare’s 14-URL corpus (medians of five Quick Action runs), Kitesurf used 380 ms CPU per screenshot vs 1,173 ms for Chromium (3.1× less) and 229 ms vs 877 ms for HTML extraction (3.8× less) . Memory dropped from 271.0 MiB to 57.8 MiB for screenshots (4.7×) and from 273.7 MiB to 39.4 MiB for extraction (7.0×) . Chromium remains faster on wall time: Kitesurf is 1.8× slower on screenshots and 1.7× slower on extraction, mostly in rasterization and image encoding. Since memory and CPU drive the bill, the trade favors bursty agent workloads. It also runs Doom. How to Use It, and Current Limits Existing Puppeteer , Playwright , chrome-remote-interface, and MCP clients work unchanged. Add browser=kitesurf to the Browser Run CDP endpoint or Quick Actions API. A public playground with injected Chrome DevTools shows DOM, console, network, and per-isolate WebAssembly memory. Kitesurf already renders TodoMVC (vanilla, React, Vue, Angular, Preact), Wikipedia, and Hacker News. Cloudflare plans to open source Kitesurf so customers can deploy their own instances. Key Takeaways Kitesurf is Cloudflare’s agent-first browser running fully in V8 isolates on Workers, free in beta. It uses 3.1–3.8× less CPU and 4.7–7.0× less memory than Chromium on common agent tasks. Chromium is still ~1.7–1.8× faster on wall time; Kitesurf wins on cost per session. Existing Puppeteer/Playwright/CDP clients work by adding a single browser=kitesurf parameter. No video, WebGL, TLS-fingerprint bot challenges, or persistent authenticated sessions yet. Check out the Technical details . Also, feel free to follow us on Twitter and don’t forget to join our 150k+ML SubReddit and Subscribe to our Newsletter . Wait! are you on telegram? now you can join us on telegram as well. Need to partner with us for promoting your GitHub Repo OR Hugging Face Page OR Product Release OR Webinar etc.? It enforces CORS, injects browser-shaped headers, keeps per-page cookie jars, and returns a 403 for anything violating policy.

WPT coverage grows by hundreds of passing tests weekly. On Cloudflare’s 14-URL corpus (medians of five Quick Action runs), Kitesurf used 380 ms CPU per screenshot vs 1,173 ms for Chromium (3.1× less) and 229 ms vs 877 ms for HTML extraction (3.8× less). Memory dropped from 271.0 MiB to 57.8 MiB for screenshots (4.7×) and from 273.7 MiB to 39.4 MiB for extraction (7.0×). Chromium remains faster on wall time: Kitesurf is 1.8× slower on screenshots and 1.7× slower on extraction, mostly in rasterization and image encoding. Since memory and CPU drive the bill, the trade favors bursty agent workloads. It also runs Doom.

How to Use It, and Current Limits

Existing Puppeteer, Playwright, chrome-remote-interface, and MCP clients work unchanged. Add browser=kitesurf to the Browser Run CDP endpoint or Quick Actions API. A public playground with injected Chrome DevTools shows DOM, console, network, and per-isolate WebAssembly memory. Kitesurf already renders TodoMVC (vanilla, React, Vue, Angular, Preact), Wikipedia, and Hacker News. Cloudflare plans to open source Kitesurf so customers can deploy their own instances.

Key Takeaways
  • Kitesurf is Cloudflare’s agent-first browser running fully in V8 isolates on Workers, free in beta.
  • It uses 3.1–3.8× less CPU and 4.7–7.0× less memory than Chromium on common agent tasks.
  • Chromium is still ~1.7–1.8× faster on wall time; Kitesurf wins on cost per session.
  • Existing Puppeteer/Playwright/CDP clients work by adding a single browser=kitesurf parameter.
  • No video, WebGL, TLS-fingerprint bot challenges, or persistent authenticated sessions yet.

Check out the Technical details. Also, feel free to follow us on Twitter and don’t forget to join our 150k+ML SubReddit and Subscribe to our Newsletter. Wait! are you on telegram? now you can join us on telegram as well.

Teams testing prompts in ChatGPT before moving them to Codex or Work may notice the difference on longer tasks.

OpenAI announced Thursday that it has updated GPT-5.6 Sol inside consumer ChatGPT while leaving the versions used by Codex and ChatGPT Work alone.

“Because this version of GPT‑5.6 Sol is optimized for everyday chats, it will only be available in the Chat experience in ChatGPT,” OpenAI said in its announcement. “The version of GPT‑5.6 Sol that powers Work and Codex is not changing as part of this release.”

“The version of GPT‑5.6 Sol that powers Work and Codex is not changing as part of this release.”

Same name, different model

ChatGPT has always handled things a bit differently from other environments. Now, those differences might become even more obvious. But the only way to know is to test prompts where they’ll actually run. There’s nothing in the announcement about changes to the GPT-5.6 Sol API model. So, it’s too soon to guess what this means for the API.

A slider replaces separate models

Because ChatGPT now uses the same Sol model for quick answers and deeper dives, Plus and Pro users get a new slider — that works on web, mobile, and desktop — to choose how much thought ChatGPT puts into an answer. Developers already make this call with the API. But they’ll still have to decide when the better answer is worth waiting and paying for.

But they’ll still have to decide when the better answer is worth waiting and paying for.

Classifiers monitor every answer

OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 System Card, published in July, indicates that Sol and Terra are paired with classifiers that monitor an answer as it is being generated. If one detects a problem, the answer is held while another system checks it. OpenAI tunes those classifiers separately for each model.

The System Card also flags a problem developers may recognize: GPT-5.6 sometimes went beyond the assignment and attempted changes the user had not requested. It did this more often than GPT-5.5, although OpenAI said it was still rare.

Benchmarks without baselines

OpenAI says the updated Sol makes fewer factual mistakes. In its internal tests of financial, medical, and legal questions, answers containing at least one error were 68% less common than those produced by GPT-5.5 Instant. Luna, which will become the default for Free and Go users, reduced errors by about 62%.

But OpenAI didn’t release the prompts or enough detail for anyone to reproduce those results. It also compared the new Sol with GPT-5.5 Instant, rather than the previous version of Sol in ChatGPT. That makes it impossible to tell how much Sol itself has improved.

That makes it impossible to tell how much Sol itself has improved.

Engineering teams will need to find out for themselves by testing prompts where they’ll actually run.  Saving that configuration with each prompt will make the results easier to reproduce — and reveal whether an upgrade on paper produces better results in practice.
